subject: Processing locus, subprocessors & export-control evidence for Medivex
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medivex.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <t.hsu@medivex.com>
Date: 2028-07-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Processing footprint & subprocessors — quick Qs

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo earlier. Our security team sent over a short questionnaire (attached) focused on where customer requests are executed, which subprocessors are involved, and cross-border transfer controls. Two quick items before we dig in: 

- Can you confirm which cloud regions/locations handle inference execution for the hosted API (and any differences for Dedicated/Private)?
- Which named subprocessors might see payloads or telemetry in a standard hosted deployment? Are there EU-only or APAC-only options?

We also flagged export-control questions — if you can point us to an evidence pack or a one-page summary that covers residency, KMS options, and whether we can pin workloads to a region, that would be great.

I've attached the questionnaire (small xlsx). Appreciate a call if it's easier.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Security Lead, Medivex Health
lena.ortiz@medivex.com

Attachment: medivex-security-questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medivex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-10T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Processing footprint & subprocessors — quick Qs

Hi Lena — thanks for sending this over and for the time today. Attaching a short processing map (PDF) and a one-page summary below. High level answers up front:

- Hosted API: primary execution occurs in our US region (us-east-1), with optional EU region (eu-west-3) for EU tenants. We do not persist request payloads beyond the configured retention window unless customer opts-in for logging.
- Dedicated: tenants get reserved GPU pools in a single region you select; we can pin to any supported region (US/EU/APAC) with contractual commitments.
- Private: full private deployment (VPC/on-prem) — you control the execution locus.

Subprocessors (hosted mode, common):
- Cloud infra: AWS (primary: us-east-1), GCP (for some embedding/replica routing), and a small EU subset for eu tenants.
- Observability & metrics: Datadog (ingests aggregated telemetry only; no raw prompts).
- Logging/ingest: S3-compatible stores for short-term caching (encrypted).

We can provide a redacted subprocessor roster and SOC2 evidence; attached PDF includes a concise processing map and a checklist of controls. If Medivex needs all processing fixed in the EU, we can propose EU-only hosting or Private deployment options.

Next steps: I can schedule a 30-min technical evidence call with our reliability lead (Connor) and security SME (Marissa) to walk the questionnaire line-by-line. Are you available Wednesday 7/12 or Thursday 7/13?

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Exec — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

Attachment: redwood-processing-map.pdf (pdf, 160KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-10T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Processing footprint & subprocessors — quick Qs

Marissa / Connor — looping you in. Medivex (security lead Lena) asked for a bit more granularity than usual: they want named subprocessors and an export-controls statement plus evidence that we can pin to region (or offer Private).

Key asks we should prepare for the call:
- A redacted subprocessor list with territories for each (which regions their infra sits in).
- One-paragraph export-control note: whether any request data may transit through non-controlled jurisdictions in the hosted flow (short answer: transient hops may occur for routing/replication; we have contractual guarantees and fallbacks).
- Confirmation of KMS/HSM options and where keys are located for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
- For EU-only requirement: what is the SLA/lead time and any cost delta to bind execution to EU-only for their Dedicated contract.

I'll propose Wed 7/12 10:00am PT — Connor, can you join to explain runtime routing and KV cache behavior? Marissa, can you bring the SOC2 redaction and any specific export-control language we typically provide?

Thanks,
Ben

Onboarding notes: keep responses tight, avoid implying absolute guarantees for multi-region replication without a contractual pin. We should surface the Private option early if they insist on zero cross-border transit.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medivex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Tom Hsu <t.hsu@medivex.com>
Date: 2028-07-10T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Processing footprint & subprocessors — quick Qs

Hi Lena — quick follow-up with the items we discussed. Short, actionable answers plus attachments: redwood-processing-map.pdf (map + subprocessor matrix) and an initial redacted subprocessor roster.

Answers:
1) Where requests execute: Hosted runs in the region associated with your tenant (default us-east-1 for US accounts). For EU customers we operate eu-west-3; APAC options exist via Dedicated/Private deployments only.

2) Subprocessors that may process transit or telemetry: AWS (us-east-1), Google Cloud (europe-west3 for certain embedding routes), HashiCorp (secrets storage for some internal ops), Datadog (aggregate metrics). We do not send raw prompt text to Datadog; logs are sampled and redacted. The attached roster shows which subprocessors see what class of data.

3) Cross-border transfers / export controls: In hosted mode transient routing can route requests through intermediate regions for operational resilience and caching; we maintain contractual constraints and monitoring to prevent long-term storage outside the tenant region. If export-control constraints require absolute locality we recommend Dedicated with EU pinning or Private deployment (both supported; Private gives you full control of network egress).

4) KMS / key custody: Hosted offers customer-managed KMS via BYOK (bring-your-own-key) in supported regions; Dedicated supports customer KMS with HSM integrations; Private supports on-prem HSMs. Keys can be kept in-region per contractual request.

Next steps:
- I attached the map and redacted roster.
- Proposed evidence call: Wed 2028-07-12 10:00 PT. Connor + Marissa will join to walk the questionnaire and provide SOC2 redaction.

If you'd prefer we can instead provide a documented export-control statement for your legal team to review prior to the call.

Best regards,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Exec — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments: redwood-processing-map.pdf, medivex-subprocessor-roster-redacted.xlsx
